events.title: Jacksonville's Norman Studios: Movie Posters from the Permanent Collection
events.description:
This exhibition was organized by the Cummer Museum of Art & Gardens. 
Before Hollywood dominated the film industry, Florida was the hot spot for movie executives. With our warm weather, sunny skies, convenient location, cheap labor, and diverse scenery, Florida quickly became a frontrunner in the early film business in the first part of the 20th century. Jacksonville in particular seemed a logical choice as a capital. The city was the principal financial, manufacturing, distribution, and transportation gateway in the Southeast. It was, in fact, the largest metropolis in the state. Its proximity to the St. Johns River, Atlantic Ocean, and Eastern railroad allowed easy access for crews and materials. At the same time, numerous environments including beaches, swamps, river views, downtown districts, and historic St. Augustine were also convenient. 
However, the heyday was short-lived. By 1920, Hollywood had already gained preeminence as the nation’s film capital. This shift westward allowed First Coast native and silent filmmaker, Richard Norman, the opportunity to purchase the bankrupt Eagle Studios complex in Arlington in 1920. Norman produced at least 8 feature films in 8 years and gained national attention by producing films with Black casts for Black audiences. 
In the earliest years of filmmaking, Black actors and actresses played extras or bit parts in films aimed toward white markets. Heroic or positive roles were unheard of until white filmmakers realized that there was a market for race-based pictures. After his purchase of the former Eagle Studios complex, Richard Norman, a white man, had the finest studio complex of any African American-based film producer. 
Norman succeeded at producing low budget yet polished and entertaining black cast films. His productions featured black actors as cowboys, pilots, and businessmen in romance, mystery, and action films. He recruited some of the most prominent stage actors to make the switch to the screen. Although his films were popular with audiences across the country, especially the emerging black middle class, he was forced to close his business at the onset of the Great Depression. 
All five buildings of the Eagle/Norman property are still standing today on Arlington Road near Cesery Boulevard and a local nonprofit, the Norman Studios Silent Film Museum, Inc., was formed in 2007 to celebrate the role of filmmaker Richard Norman in the early days of the movie industry. The site is listed in the National Register of Historic Places. 
*Unless otherwise noted, these posters were purchased in 2002 with funds provided by the Morton R. Hirschberg Memorial Fund, Mr. Moselle C. Bruton, Ms. Janet R. Johnson, Mr. Michael Lewis, Dr. Emma Moran, Dr. and Mrs. Joseph Anello, Ms. Thelma Geiger and Mrs. Gloriden J. Norris.

events.title: Revisiting Christian Iconography
events.description:
Revisiting Christian Iconography asks the viewer to consider how traditional Christian artwork and iconography has changed across time. Scenes depicting the life of Jesus Christ, the Virgin Mary, or other New Testament references have been used for centuries in Western European art to inspire devotion. However, as artistic self-expression became more prevalent in the late 19th and early 20th centuries, artists such as Abraham Rattner and Marc Chagall used Biblical references to expand on universal themes. While rooted in tradition, these modern works challenge the imagination, encouraging reverence for the sacred and contemplation of the transcendent. 
Presented by The Edge Family

events.title: Touring the Landscape: Art, Travel and the Shaping of American Identity
events.description:
Touring the Landscape explores how American artists of the late 19th and early 20th centuries shaped national identity through landscape paintings of iconic tourist destinations. As a burgeoning tourist industry grew, artists traveled widely, shaping a corpus of iconic views that helped define what it meant to be American. 
From the marshes of Florida to the pastoral hills of New England, from the dramatic peaks of the American West to the scenic landscapes of Italy, the paintings in this exhibition reflect an evolving relationship between people and place. In a time of expansion, conflict, and industrialization, they reveal how a shared visual experience of landscape became central to the American imagination and the broader project of nationhood. 
This exhibition, assembled from the Cummer Museum’s permanent collection, is guest curated by University of North Florida students in Dr. Meg McCrummen Fowler’s class, “Public Narratives: Museum Curation and Interpretation.” 
The Cummer Museum has received the Southeastern Museums Conference (SEMC) Exhibition Bronze Award in recognition of the exhibition Touring the Landscape: Art, Travel, and the Shaping of American Identity. The SEMC Exhibition Competition showcases the best in our profession and provides benchmarks for regional exhibition efforts in southeastern museums.

events.title: Ashley Woodson Bailey: What Remains
events.description:
The Cummer Museum’s Bank of America Concourse Gallery welcomes Jacksonville-based photographer and artist Ashley Woodson Bailey with What Remains. This body of work explores the relationship between photography, time, and preservation through the botanical subject. 
“Flowers have long functioned as a visual language in art, symbolizing beauty, mortality, and transformation,” Bailey shares. “I am drawn to the tension between fragility and permanence—how something inherently fleeting can be held, altered, and re-seen.” 
In What Remains, floral photographs are presented alongside translucent grasscloth panels, shifting wallpaper from decorative surface into something closer to a preserved specimen. The photographs function as both record and memory, while the textile panels emphasize physical presence, moving the work between image and object. 
In dialogue with Moment in Time, A Legacy of Photographs and Art in Bloom, What Remains reflects on how artists attempt to hold onto beauty and how every act of preservation inevitably transforms what it seeks to save.

Make & Take classes offer an introductory hands-on experience for visitors who want to try a new technique in a relaxed, welcoming environment. In these sessions, participants receive a brief overview of materials and techniques, then focus on guided experimentation and completing a project to take home.
 

These classes are ideal for beginners, curious learners, and anyone looking to try something new. They are designed for creative exploration and do not include advanced instruction or extended skill development.
 

Looking to go deeper? Explore our Workshops for extended learning, deeper technique, and more in-depth instruction.

events.title: Space Tech in Jax
events.description:
JAX Women In Technology
**\*\*\* RSVP: [https://www.meetup.com/jax-tech-meetup/events/315806240/](https://www.meetup.com/jax-tech-meetup/events/315806240/) \*\*\***

Did you know Jacksonville and North Florida are home to a thriving and rapidly growing space entrepreneurship ecosystem? Neither did a lot of people, but that's exactly what we're here to change.

For our Q3 event, Jax Tech is heading to the final frontier. We're bringing together founders, scientists, marketers, and researchers who are actively building the future of space right here in our backyard, and far beyond it.

From power grid infrastructure orbiting Earth to the fastest-growing sector you've never heard of, this event will open your eyes to just how much is happening in the space industry, and how close to home it all is.

Whether you're an entrepreneur, a technologist, an astropreneur, a curious skeptic, or someone who's always dreamed of what comes next for humanity beyond our atmosphere, you won't want to miss this one.

### **Featured Speakers**

#### **Camille Elizabeth Bergin**

**Chief Marketing Officer\, Star Catcher \| @TheGalacticGal**
Camille will set the stage for the evening with a sweeping look at the space industry: what it actually is today, where it's headed, and why now is such a pivotal moment. Known across the industry as The Galactic Gal, Camille brings a rare combination of deep technical knowledge and the ability to make it all make sense.
She'll explore:

* What the modern space industry really looks like — and why it's bigger than most people realize
* How satellites are quietly driving payments, communications, and critical infrastructure here on Earth
* The rise of manufacturing in space and what it means for the broader economy
* What's happening on the moon, and what comes after that

Expect an engaging, big-picture orientation that will frame everything else you'll hear that evening.

#### **Andrew Rush**

**Co-Founder & CEO, Star Catcher**
Andrew is a serial entrepreneur in the space sector, right here in Jacksonville. As CEO of Star Catcher, he's leading one of the most exciting space startups in the country: a company building power grid infrastructure for space itself.
He'll share:

* The Star Catcher story and their upcoming launch
* The state of the space industry from an operator's perspective — who the key players are and where the real action is happening
* What it looks like to build and scale a venture-backed space company
* Where he sees the industry going and what that means for entrepreneurs paying attention right now

If you've ever wondered what it takes to build a company that literally operates in orbit, Andrew's session will give you a front-row seat.

#### **Sierra Pollard, Ph.D.**

**Director, Space Innovation, University of Florida**
The space economy isn't just for astronauts and aerospace giants, and Dr. Pollard has made it her mission to prove that. As Director of Space Innovation at UF, she works at the intersection of opportunities in education, NASA technology pipeline, and the next generation of entrepreneurs ready to commercialize it.
She'll cover:

* NASA tech transfer programs and how entrepreneurs can access and license space technologies
* Building a business around the space economy
* Space hospitality: the fastest-growing sector in the industry you haven't heard enough about yet
* VAST and the emerging category of hotels and habitation in space
* What the on-ramp to space entrepreneurship actually looks like today

This is a session for anyone who's ever thought "there has to be an opportunity here"...because there absolutely is, and Dr. Pollard will show you where to start.

After the sessions, join us for the rooftop afterparty with DJ Castronaut spinning beats and great conversations with some of the most interesting people in the Jacksonville tech scene. Bartenders from **The Volstead** will be back to keep the energy going.
As always, a HUGE thank you to our sponsors that make these events possible:

* Harbor View Advisors ([https://www.harborviewadvisors.com/](https://www.harborviewadvisors.com/)) — Helping Jacksonville investors and founders connect and thrive, through sell-side and buy-side advisory and consulting
* ForSale by Plus ([https://www.forsalebypl.us/](https://www.forsalebypl.us/)) — Finding and selling homes in Jacksonville, and spinning DJ tunes on the MOSH rooftop

Join us every Monday for a meaningful Philosophy Book Club as we explore *Meditations* by Marcus Aurelius, one of the most influential works of Stoic philosophy.

More than a book to be read, *Meditations* is an invitation to reflect on how we live. Together, we'll explore timeless questions about self-mastery, resilience, purpose, relationships, and how to face life's challenges with greater wisdom and inner strength.
Our meetings are open conversations where we connect Marcus Aurelius' reflections with our own experiences and everyday life.

events.title: Tiffany or Ti-phony? A Story of Desire
events.description:
Featuring 45 lamps from The Neustadt’s renowned collection, Tiffany or Tiphony? starts with a seemingly simple question—is a lamp genuine Tiffany or a deliciously deceptive Ti-phony? This exhibition sheds light on an unexpected tale of innovation, desire, and imitation. Exciting new research, careful comparison, and engaging interactive elements offer a fresh and fascinating perspective on these beloved artworks. By learning to look closely, visitors will uncover clues to the lamps’ true identities and discover why it’s important (and fun!) to spot a fake. 
Organized by The Neustadt Collection of Tiffany Glass, Queens, New York.

The gathering provides an informal environment to network, share insights, discuss career development, and explore trends shaping the tech landscape.

Attendees have the opportunity to exchange experiences, learn from one another, and build supportive relationships within the Jacksonville tech community. The meetup’s relaxed format encourages open dialogue and collaboration while fostering a sense of inclusion and professional growth for all participants.

Recruiters are always welcome and encouraged to come. We also decide where we would like to go for future lunches in addition to topics of interest for future meetings as well.
